lessons.title: Filestore
lessons.what: Managed NFS file shares for VMs and GKE.
lessons.tests: when an application needs a shared POSIX file system, for example a lift-and-shift app, media rendering or GKE ReadWriteMany volumes.
rules: Tiers range from basic HDD and SSD to zonal and regional (enterprise) for higher availability.
Mounted over NFS by many VMs or Pods at the same time; capacity is provisioned up front.
Use Cloud Storage instead when the app can work with objects over an API: it is cheaper and scales without provisioning.
traps: Cloud Storage for an app that needs a mounted shared file system
Filestore
Cloud Storage is object storage reached by API. Apps that expect a shared file system need NFS.
Filestore to serve images to web users
Cloud Storage, with Cloud CDN
Filestore is mounted by servers. Web delivery is cheaper and faster from Cloud Storage with CDN.
A self-managed NFS server on a VM
Filestore
A self-run NFS server means patching, backups and high-availability work. Filestore is managed.

lessons.title: Data Transfer Services
lessons.what: Tools for moving data into Google Cloud: `gcloud storage`, Storage Transfer Service, Transfer Appliance and BigQuery Data Transfer Service.
lessons.tests: which transfer tool fits the size, source, network and schedule.
rules: `gcloud storage` for small or one-off copies (roughly under 1 TB) from on-premises or between buckets.
Storage Transfer Service for large or recurring transfers from other clouds, HTTP sources or on-premises file systems (with agents), with scheduling and incremental copies.
Transfer Appliance, a physical device, when the link is slow or the data is tens of terabytes or more. BigQuery Data Transfer Service schedules loads from SaaS apps, Amazon S3 and other warehouses.
traps: Write a script to copy 200 TB from Amazon S3
Storage Transfer Service
Scripts don't retry, schedule or verify well at this size. Storage Transfer Service is managed and resumable.
Ship disks yourself for 500 TB
Transfer Appliance
Transfer Appliance is Google's secure, encrypted way to ship large data offline.
A custom loader for daily Google Ads data into BigQuery
BigQuery Data Transfer Service
BigQuery Data Transfer Service already has scheduled connectors for Google Ads and other sources.

domains.title: Database Services
domains.sub: Relational, NoSQL and in-memory databases, and the line between them.

lessons.title: Cloud SQL
lessons.what: Managed MySQL, PostgreSQL and SQL Server. Google handles backups, patching, replication and failover.
lessons.tests: when the scenario needs a standard relational database in one region, or a lift-and-shift of MySQL, PostgreSQL or SQL Server.
rules: High availability: a standby in another zone of the same region with synchronous replication and automatic failover. The standby does not serve reads.
Read replicas (in-region or cross-region) offload reads and can be promoted manually for disaster recovery. Writes scale only vertically.
Point-in-time recovery needs automated backups and binary logging (or WAL). Connect with the Cloud SQL Auth Proxy or connectors, preferably over private IP.
traps: Read replicas for automatic failover
The HA configuration (regional standby)
Read replicas don't fail over automatically. The HA standby does.
Cloud SQL for a global app needing writes in several regions
Spanner
Cloud SQL writes go to one regional primary. Spanner accepts writes across regions.
Open the database to 0.0.0.0/0 so Cloud Run can connect
Private IP with the Cloud SQL connector or Auth Proxy
A public database endpoint invites attacks. Private IP with the connector keeps traffic internal and encrypted.

lessons.title: AlloyDB for PostgreSQL
lessons.what: A PostgreSQL-compatible managed database built for demanding workloads, with a built-in columnar engine for fast analytics on live data.
lessons.tests: when a PostgreSQL workload has outgrown Cloud SQL in performance or needs analytics on transactional data (HTAP).
rules: Fully PostgreSQL-compatible, so apps and tools move without changes.
Primary instance plus read pool instances; regional high availability with a 99.99% SLA.
The columnar engine speeds up analytical queries without copying data to a warehouse; AlloyDB Omni runs the same engine on-premises or in other clouds.
traps: Spanner for a single-region PostgreSQL app that needs more speed
AlloyDB
Spanner is for global scale and needs schema changes. AlloyDB is a faster PostgreSQL with no rewrite.
Copy operational data to BigQuery for every quick report
AlloyDB's columnar engine for analytics on live data
Copying adds pipelines and delay. The columnar engine answers analytics on live data.
Rewrite the app to move from PostgreSQL to AlloyDB
No rewrite needed; it is PostgreSQL-compatible
AlloyDB speaks PostgreSQL, so apps connect as before.

lessons.title: Spanner
lessons.what: A globally distributed relational database with strong consistency, SQL, and horizontal scaling of both reads and writes.
lessons.tests: when the scenario needs relational data with global scale, very high availability (up to 99.999%) or more write throughput than one machine gives.
rules: Regional configurations give 99.99%; multi-region configurations give 99.999%. Capacity is set in nodes or processing units and can change without downtime.
Avoid hotspots: do not use monotonically increasing primary keys such as timestamps or sequences; use UUIDs or hashed keys. Interleave child tables with parents for locality.
Supports GoogleSQL and a PostgreSQL interface; use Dataflow or the console for exports.
traps: Auto-increment primary keys in Spanner
UUIDs or hashed keys to spread writes
Sequential keys send every new write to the same split, creating a hotspot.
Spanner for a small regional app on a tight budget
Cloud SQL
Spanner's cost and design effort aren't justified for a small regional app.
Shard Cloud SQL by hand to scale writes
Spanner scales writes horizontally
Manual sharding is complex and fragile. Spanner shards automatically.

lessons.title: Firestore
lessons.what: A serverless NoSQL document database with real-time updates, offline support for mobile and web, and ACID transactions. Datastore mode is the older API.
lessons.tests: when the scenario needs a flexible schema for user profiles, catalogues, game state or mobile and web apps, with no servers to manage.
rules: Serverless: scales automatically, pay per read, write and storage; regional or multi-region.
Strongly consistent queries with indexes; no joins, so model data the way the app reads it.
Client libraries sync data in real time and work offline on mobile and web.
traps: Firestore for complex joins and analytics
BigQuery (export Firestore data to it)
Firestore has no joins and isn't built for heavy aggregation. Export to BigQuery for analysis.
Firestore for billions of time-series writes a day
Bigtable
Bigtable handles very high write rates by key more cheaply.
Cloud SQL for a fast-changing schema in a mobile app
Firestore
A rigid schema slows frequent changes. Documents can gain fields without migrations.

lessons.title: Bigtable
lessons.what: A wide-column NoSQL database for very large, high-throughput workloads with low-latency reads and writes by key. HBase API compatible.
lessons.tests: when the scenario has IoT or time-series data, ad tech, financial ticks, or more than about a terabyte with millions of operations per second.
rules: Only one index, the row key: design it around the main query, avoid keys that start with a timestamp or sequence, and use reverse timestamps to read the latest first.
Single-row transactions only. Add nodes to scale with no downtime; add clusters in other zones or regions for replication and failover, routed by app profiles.
Use SSD storage for most cases, HDD only for large, rarely read data. The command-line tool is `cbt`.
traps: Row keys that start with a timestamp
Start with an identifier (device ID), then a (reversed) timestamp
Keys that start with a timestamp send all new writes to one node. Leading with an ID spreads them.
Bigtable for multi-row transactions
Spanner or Cloud SQL
Bigtable only guarantees atomic changes within one row.
Bigtable for ad hoc SQL analysis
BigQuery, which can also query Bigtable
Bigtable has no engine for ad hoc SQL. BigQuery can query Bigtable data.

lessons.title: Memorystore
lessons.what: Managed in-memory data stores: Redis (and Valkey) and Memcached.
lessons.tests: when the scenario needs sub-millisecond reads: caching query results, sessions, leaderboards or rate limits.
rules: Redis supports persistence, replication and high availability (Standard tier with a replica and automatic failover); Memcached is a simple, multi-node cache.
Put a cache in front of a database to cut read load and latency; move session state out of VMs into Memorystore so the app can scale horizontally.
Reach it over private IP from Compute Engine, GKE, Cloud Run and App Engine in the same VPC.
traps: Memcached when the data must survive a restart
Redis with persistence
Memcached keeps data only in memory and loses it on restart.
Memorystore as the only copy of order data
A database as the source of truth, with Memorystore as a cache
A cache can evict or lose data. The database must hold the authoritative copy.
Sticky sessions on VMs to keep user sessions
Store sessions in Memorystore
Sticky sessions break when a VM goes away. Shared session storage lets any instance serve any user.

domains.title: Networking Services
domains.sub: Virtual networks, load balancing, content delivery, DNS and connections to other networks.

lessons.title: Virtual Private Cloud (VPC)
lessons.what: Your private, global network in Google Cloud, with regional subnets, routes and firewall rules.
lessons.tests: how to lay out networks, share them across projects and control traffic between workloads.
rules: Use custom-mode VPCs with planned, non-overlapping ranges; add secondary ranges for GKE Pods and Services.
Shared VPC lets one host project own the network that many service projects use; VPC Network Peering connects separate networks and is not transitive.
Firewall rules use tags or service accounts as targets; hierarchical firewall policies apply rules across an organisation or folder. VPC Flow Logs help troubleshooting.
traps: Peering A to B and B to C lets A reach C
Peering is not transitive; peer A and C directly or use Network Connectivity Center
Peering only connects the two networks named. Traffic doesn't pass through a network in the middle.
Copy the same firewall rule into every project
A hierarchical firewall policy at the organisation or folder
Copies drift and are easy to miss. One policy at the top applies everywhere below it.
The default network for production
A custom-mode VPC
The default network has auto-created subnets and loose rules. Custom mode gives planned ranges and tighter control.

lessons.title: Cloud Load Balancing
lessons.what: Fully managed, software-defined load balancers, global or regional, external or internal.
lessons.tests: which load balancer fits the traffic type, scope and features.
rules: Application Load Balancer (Layer 7, HTTP and HTTPS): URL maps for host and path routing, weighted traffic splits, Cloud CDN, Cloud Armor and IAP. External global, regional or internal.
Proxy Network Load Balancer (Layer 4 TCP, with optional TLS offload) and passthrough Network Load Balancer (TCP and UDP, keeps the client IP, lowest latency).

A global external load balancer gives one anycast IP that routes users to the nearest healthy region; it needs Premium Tier networking. Backends can be MIGs, NEGs (Pods, serverless, hybrid) or buckets.
traps: Network load balancer for path routing
Application Load Balancer
Only Layer 7 load balancers can read URLs and hostnames.
Application Load Balancer for a UDP game server
Passthrough Network Load Balancer
Application Load Balancers handle HTTP and HTTPS only. UDP needs a network load balancer.
Global single anycast IP on Standard Tier
Premium Tier networking
Standard Tier uses regional IPs. Global anycast routing needs Premium Tier.

lessons.title: Cloud CDN
lessons.what: Caches content at Google's edge, close to users, behind an external Application Load Balancer.
lessons.tests: when the scenario needs faster global delivery of static or cacheable content and less load on the origin.
rules: Origins can be Cloud Storage buckets, instance groups, Cloud Run and other serverless backends, or external origins.
Control caching with Cache-Control headers and cache keys; use versioned file names instead of frequent invalidations; protect private content with signed URLs or cookies.
Media CDN is the option for large-scale video streaming.
traps: A bigger origin to serve global static assets
Cloud CDN in front of the origin
A bigger origin still leaves distant users with high latency. Edge caches serve them from nearby.
Invalidate the cache on every release
Versioned URLs (app.v2.js)
Invalidations are slow and limited. New file names make the CDN and browsers fetch the new version at once.
Cache pages containing patient data
Do not cache sensitive or personal responses
Cached personal data could reach the wrong user and breaks compliance rules.

lessons.title: Cloud DNS
lessons.what: Managed, authoritative DNS with a 100% availability SLA, for public and private zones.
lessons.tests: how names resolve on the internet, inside VPCs and across hybrid networks.
rules: Public zones serve the internet; private zones serve only chosen VPC networks.
Hybrid DNS: forwarding zones send queries to on-premises DNS; inbound server policies let on-premises systems resolve Google Cloud names; DNS peering shares zones between VPCs.
Routing policies (weighted, geolocation, failover) steer traffic; DNSSEC protects against spoofing.
traps: Public DNS records for internal service names
A private zone
Public records expose internal names and addresses to the internet.
Copy on-premises records into Cloud DNS by hand
A forwarding zone to the on-premises DNS servers
Copied records go stale. Forwarding asks the on-premises DNS directly.
Run BIND on a VM for internal names
Cloud DNS private zones
A self-run DNS server adds availability and patching work. Cloud DNS is managed with a 100% SLA.

lessons.title: Cloud VPN and Cloud Interconnect
lessons.what: Ways to connect on-premises or other clouds to a VPC: encrypted tunnels over the internet, or private physical links.
lessons.tests: which connection meets the bandwidth, SLA, privacy and cost needs.
rules: HA VPN: two interfaces, 99.99% SLA, dynamic routing with Cloud Router (BGP), encrypted, about 3 Gbps per tunnel. Classic VPN is the older 99.9% option.

Dedicated Interconnect: 10 or 100 Gbps circuits in a colocation facility. Partner Interconnect: 50 Mbps to 50 Gbps through a provider when you cannot reach a facility. Cross-Cloud Interconnect links to other clouds.
Interconnect traffic is private but not encrypted by default; add MACsec or HA VPN over Interconnect when encryption is required. Keep a backup connection.
traps: HA VPN for 20 Gbps of steady replication
Dedicated Interconnect
Each VPN tunnel tops out around 3 Gbps over the internet. Interconnect gives dedicated high bandwidth.
Assume Interconnect traffic is encrypted
Add MACsec or HA VPN over Interconnect
Interconnect is private but not encrypted by default. Compliance may require MACsec or VPN on top.
Dedicated Interconnect from a site far from any colocation facility
Partner Interconnect
Dedicated Interconnect needs presence in a colocation facility. A partner extends the link to you.

lessons.title: Cloud NAT, Private Google Access and Private Service Connect
lessons.what: Ways for private workloads to reach the internet, Google APIs and managed services without public IPs.
lessons.tests: how a workload with no external IP gets the access it needs.
rules: Cloud NAT gives outbound internet access (updates, external APIs) to VMs and GKE nodes with only internal IPs; nothing can connect inbound through it.
Private Google Access lets internal-only VMs call Google APIs such as Cloud Storage and BigQuery.

Private Service Connect reaches Google APIs, managed services and services published by other teams or companies through private endpoints in your VPC. Private services access gives Cloud SQL and Memorystore private IPs.
traps: External IPs so private VMs can download patches
Cloud NAT
External IPs expose VMs to inbound traffic. Cloud NAT allows outbound only.
Cloud NAT so private VMs can reach Cloud Storage
Private Google Access
Google APIs can be reached privately with Private Google Access, without going out to the internet.
VPC peering to consume a partner's service in another organisation
Private Service Connect
Peering joins whole networks and needs non-overlapping ranges. Private Service Connect exposes just one service.

domains.title: Security and Identity Services
domains.sub: Who can do what, keys and secrets, and the services that protect apps and data.

lessons.title: IAM and Resource Manager
lessons.what: Identity and Access Management decides who can do what on which resource; Resource Manager holds the organisation, folders and projects that policies attach to.
lessons.tests: where to grant access, which kind of role to use, and how to find and remove excess access.
rules: Policies bind principals (users, groups, service accounts) to roles at the organisation, folder, project or resource; children inherit them. IAM conditions limit access by time, resource name or tag.
Deny policies block a permission even when a role grants it; organisation policies restrict configurations (regions, external IPs, key creation).
Role recommendations flag unused permissions; Policy Troubleshooter explains why someone has or lacks access; Policy Analyzer answers who can access what.
traps: Grant Owner so a contractor can view everything
Viewer, or a narrow predefined role
Owner can change and delete everything. Viewing only needs Viewer or a narrower role.
Guess why access is denied
Policy Troubleshooter
Policy Troubleshooter checks every policy on the path and names the missing permission.
Temporary access by remembering to remove it
An IAM condition with an expiry time
People forget. A time-based condition removes the access automatically.

lessons.title: Cloud Identity, Federation and Identity Platform
lessons.what: Cloud Identity manages the users and groups that sign in to Google Cloud. Federation lets them use an existing identity provider. Identity Platform signs in your app's customers.
lessons.tests: how employees and partners sign in, and how that differs from customer sign-in.
rules: Keep Active Directory as the source: Google Cloud Directory Sync copies users and groups one way into Cloud Identity, and SSO (SAML or OIDC through AD FS, Entra ID or Okta) handles passwords.
Workforce Identity Federation lets users from an external identity provider use Google Cloud without syncing accounts.
Identity Platform adds sign-up, sign-in and multi-factor authentication for your own apps, with email, phone, social and SAML or OIDC providers.
traps: Create Google accounts by hand for 5,000 AD users
Google Cloud Directory Sync plus SSO
Manual accounts drift from Active Directory. Sync keeps users and groups in step automatically.
Sync passwords to Google
SSO keeps authentication at the identity provider
With SSO, passwords stay with your identity provider, so Google never needs a copy.
Cloud IAM users for a shopping app's customers
Identity Platform
IAM is for managing Google Cloud. Identity Platform handles your app's own sign-up and sign-in.

lessons.title: Cloud KMS, Cloud HSM and Secret Manager
lessons.what: Cloud KMS creates and controls encryption keys; Cloud HSM keeps them in hardware security modules; Secret Manager stores passwords, API keys and certificates.
lessons.tests: which key or secret service meets a control or compliance requirement.
rules: Cloud KMS: symmetric keys for CMEK with automatic rotation, asymmetric keys for signing and verification. Key destruction is scheduled, giving time to undo it.
Cloud HSM for FIPS 140-2 Level 3 hardware-backed keys; Cloud External Key Manager when keys must stay outside Google.
Secret Manager: versioned secrets, IAM per secret, audit logs, rotation reminders through Pub/Sub; apps read secrets at runtime.
traps: Software KMS keys when a regulator demands hardware-protected keys
Cloud HSM
Software keys don't meet a hardware requirement. Cloud HSM keeps keys in certified hardware.
Store keys in Cloud KMS when policy says Google must never hold them
Cloud External Key Manager
Cloud KMS and Cloud HSM keys live in Google. External Key Manager keeps them in a key manager you control.
Encrypt a database password with KMS and keep it in the repo
Secret Manager
The secret still sits in code next to the means to decrypt it. Secret Manager stores and audits it separately.

lessons.title: Cloud Armor and Identity-Aware Proxy
lessons.what: Cloud Armor is a web application firewall and DDoS defence for load balancers. Identity-Aware Proxy (IAP) checks identity and context before letting a user reach an app or VM.
lessons.tests: how to protect public apps from attacks and give staff access without a VPN or public IPs.
rules: Cloud Armor: preconfigured OWASP Top 10 rules (SQL injection, XSS), IP and geo allow and deny lists, rate limiting and Adaptive Protection, attached to backend services.
IAP for web apps behind an Application Load Balancer, Cloud Run or App Engine: access by IAM role and device or location context.
IAP TCP forwarding opens SSH and RDP to VMs with no external IP and no bastion host.
traps: A bastion host with a public IP for SSH
IAP TCP forwarding
A public bastion is one more server to attack, patch and watch. IAP tunnels SSH through Google with IAM checks.
VPC firewall rules to block SQL injection
Cloud Armor WAF rules
Firewalls see IPs and ports, not request content. Cloud Armor inspects HTTP for attack patterns.
A VPN for staff to reach one internal web app
IAP
A VPN opens the network. IAP opens just the app, per user.

lessons.title: Security Command Center, VPC Service Controls and Sensitive Data Protection
lessons.what: Security Command Center finds misconfigurations, vulnerabilities and threats. VPC Service Controls draws a perimeter around Google APIs. Sensitive Data Protection (Cloud DLP) finds and masks sensitive data.
lessons.tests: the service that gives visibility, stops data exfiltration, or handles personal data.
rules: Security Command Center: one view of findings across the organisation, such as public buckets, open firewall rules, vulnerable images and active threats.

VPC Service Controls: services such as BigQuery and Cloud Storage inside a perimeter cannot send data to projects outside it, even with valid credentials; access levels allow trusted networks or devices.

Sensitive Data Protection: discover and classify sensitive data, then de-identify it by masking, tokenising or format-preserving encryption before analysis. Assured Workloads helps with regulated data residency.
traps: Write scripts to check every project for public buckets
Security Command Center
Scripts miss new checks and new projects. Security Command Center scans the whole organisation continuously.
IAM alone to stop copying data to an outside project
VPC Service Controls
Credentials that can read data can also copy it out. A perimeter blocks the copy.
Delete all personal fields so analysts can work
De-identify with Sensitive Data Protection and keep the data useful
Deleting fields loses their value for analysis. Masking or tokenising keeps the value while protecting people.

domains.title: Data and Analytics Services
domains.sub: Warehousing, messaging, processing, orchestration and dashboards.

lessons.title: BigQuery
lessons.what: A serverless data warehouse for SQL analytics on terabytes to petabytes, with storage and compute billed separately.
lessons.tests: when the scenario needs analytics, reporting, a data warehouse, or ML with SQL.
rules: Pricing: on-demand (per TB scanned) or capacity (editions with slot reservations). Partition by date or ingestion time and cluster by common filters to scan less; tables unchanged for 90 days get cheaper long-term storage.
Load in batch for free; stream with the Storage Write API. Query data in Cloud Storage and other sources with external and BigLake tables.
Secure with dataset IAM, authorised views, row-level security and column-level policy tags. BigQuery ML trains models with SQL; time travel restores data from the last 7 days.
traps: BigQuery for a transactional order system
Cloud SQL, AlloyDB or Spanner
BigQuery is built for large scans, not many small, fast row updates.
A separate table per analyst to hide salary columns
Column-level security with policy tags, or authorised views
Copies drift and multiply storage. Policy tags or authorised views control access on one table.
`SELECT *` to preview a huge table
Table preview, or select only the columns you need
BigQuery bills by the columns scanned, so `SELECT *` reads and bills every column. Table preview is free.

lessons.title: Pub/Sub
lessons.what: A global, serverless messaging service. Publishers send to topics; subscribers receive from subscriptions.
lessons.tests: when services must be decoupled, events must be buffered, or streaming data must be ingested.
rules: Delivery is at least once by default; use ordering keys for ordered delivery and exactly-once delivery on pull subscriptions when duplicates are not allowed.
Pull, push, BigQuery and Cloud Storage subscriptions; each subscription gets every message, and several clients on one subscription share the load.
Dead-letter topics catch messages that keep failing; message retention and seek let you replay. Pub/Sub plus Dataflow is the standard streaming pipeline.
traps: Expect each message exactly once by default
Design consumers to be idempotent, or enable exactly-once delivery
Delivery is at least once, so a consumer may see a message twice.
Keep retrying a poison message forever
A dead-letter topic
A message that always fails blocks progress and wastes resources. A dead-letter topic sets it aside.
Direct synchronous calls between services during traffic spikes
Pub/Sub to buffer the load
Synchronous chains fail together under load. A queue absorbs spikes.

lessons.title: Dataflow
lessons.what: Serverless, autoscaling processing for batch and streaming pipelines, running Apache Beam.
lessons.tests: when the scenario needs new ETL, streaming analytics or one codebase for batch and streaming.
rules: Beam handles windows, watermarks and late data for streaming; Dataflow scales workers automatically and processes exactly once.
Google-provided templates cover common jobs (Pub/Sub to BigQuery, Cloud Storage text to BigQuery) without writing code.
To change a running streaming job, update it in place or drain it (finish in-flight data); cancelling stops at once and may drop data.
traps: Cancel a streaming job to deploy new code
Update the job or drain it
Cancel stops at once and may drop in-flight data. Update or drain finishes it cleanly.
Dataproc for a brand-new streaming pipeline
Dataflow
Dataproc needs clusters. Dataflow is serverless and built for streaming.
A custom app on VMs to move Pub/Sub messages into BigQuery
A Dataflow template, or a BigQuery subscription
Templates and BigQuery subscriptions do this with no code to run.

lessons.title: Dataproc
lessons.what: Managed Apache Spark, Hadoop, Hive and related open-source tools, on clusters or serverless.
lessons.tests: when the scenario has existing Spark or Hadoop jobs to move, or needs the open-source ecosystem.
rules: Clusters start in about 90 seconds, so create one per job and delete it afterwards (ephemeral clusters) rather than keeping a big cluster running.
Keep data in Cloud Storage, not HDFS, so storage outlives clusters; add Spot secondary workers to cut cost.
Dataproc Serverless runs Spark jobs with no cluster at all.
traps: Keep one large Dataproc cluster running all day for nightly jobs
Ephemeral clusters per job, or Dataproc Serverless
An always-on cluster bills while it sits idle. Ephemeral clusters or serverless cost only while jobs run.
Store data in HDFS on the cluster
Cloud Storage
HDFS data vanishes with the cluster. Cloud Storage keeps it and lets many clusters share it.
Rewrite Hadoop jobs in Beam before migrating
Move them to Dataproc as they are
Moving jobs as they are is faster and lower risk. Modernise later.

lessons.title: Cloud Composer, Workflows, Dataform and Looker
lessons.what: Orchestration and BI: Composer is managed Apache Airflow, Workflows orchestrates API calls, Dataform manages SQL transformations in BigQuery, and Looker and Looker Studio build dashboards.
lessons.tests: which tool schedules, chains or presents data work.
rules: Cloud Composer for complex, scheduled data pipelines (DAGs) across many services, including on-premises and other clouds.
Workflows for lightweight serverless orchestration of services and APIs; Cloud Scheduler for simple timed triggers.
Dataform for version-controlled SQL pipelines in BigQuery. Looker for governed metrics with a semantic model (LookML); Looker Studio for free, quick dashboards.
traps: Cron on a VM to run a 30-step data pipeline
Cloud Composer
Cron has no dependencies, retries or monitoring between steps. Composer manages the whole pipeline.
Composer to call three APIs in order once a day
Workflows with Cloud Scheduler
Composer keeps an Airflow environment running all the time. Workflows is serverless and suits short API sequences.
Each team defines revenue differently in its own dashboard
Looker with one shared semantic model
Dashboards that each define metrics differently give conflicting numbers. A shared model gives one definition.

domains.title: DevOps and Operations Services
domains.sub: Building, deploying, provisioning, observing and integrating applications.

lessons.title: Cloud Build, Artifact Registry and Cloud Deploy
lessons.what: Cloud Build runs serverless CI builds and tests; Artifact Registry stores container images and packages; Cloud Deploy delivers releases through environments.
lessons.tests: how to assemble a managed CI/CD pipeline on Google Cloud.
rules: Cloud Build runs steps from a build file, triggered by commits in GitHub, GitLab or other repositories; private pools reach resources in a private network.
Artifact Registry stores Docker images and language packages, scans for vulnerabilities and replaces Container Registry; remote repositories cache public sources.
Cloud Deploy promotes releases to GKE and Cloud Run through dev, staging and prod with approvals, canary deployments and rollbacks.
traps: Container Registry for a new project
Artifact Registry
Container Registry is retired. Artifact Registry replaces it.
A self-managed Jenkins server as the only option
Cloud Build, unless the scenario requires keeping Jenkins
Jenkins means running build servers. Cloud Build is serverless, unless the scenario says to keep existing tools.
Hand-run `kubectl` commands to promote to production
Cloud Deploy with an approval step
Manual promotion is error-prone and unaudited. Cloud Deploy adds approvals, history and rollback.

lessons.title: Terraform, Infrastructure Manager and Config Connector
lessons.what: Tools for infrastructure as code: Terraform describes resources in files; Infrastructure Manager runs Terraform as a Google Cloud service; Config Connector manages Google Cloud resources as Kubernetes objects.
lessons.tests: how to create repeatable environments and avoid configuration drift.
rules: Keep Terraform code in version control and its state in a Cloud Storage bucket (remote state with locking); review plans before applying.
Infrastructure Manager runs Terraform for you with history and IAM; Deployment Manager is the older, deprecated tool.
Change infrastructure only through the code; console edits cause drift. Config Connector suits teams that already run everything through Kubernetes and GitOps.
traps: Terraform state on a laptop
A Cloud Storage backend with locking
Local state gets lost and can't be shared. A remote backend with locking stops two people applying at once.
Deployment Manager for new projects
Terraform or Infrastructure Manager
Deployment Manager is deprecated. Terraform is Google's recommended infrastructure-as-code tool.
Fix production in the console, then forget it
Change the code and apply it
Manual changes drift from the code and get overwritten on the next apply.

lessons.title: Google Cloud Observability
lessons.what: Cloud Monitoring, Cloud Logging, Cloud Trace, Cloud Profiler and Error Reporting: metrics, logs, traces, profiles and errors in one suite.
lessons.tests: which observability service answers the question in the scenario.
rules: Cloud Monitoring: metrics scopes to view many projects, dashboards, uptime checks, SLO monitoring, alerting policies and Managed Service for Prometheus.
Cloud Logging: the Log Router sends logs to buckets, BigQuery, Cloud Storage or Pub/Sub; log-based metrics turn log lines into alertable numbers; Log Analytics queries logs with SQL.
Cloud Trace for latency across services, Cloud Profiler for CPU and memory hot spots in code, Error Reporting for grouped exceptions. Instrument with OpenTelemetry.
traps: A separate dashboard per project for one app
One metrics scope covering all its projects
Switching between projects hides the full picture. A metrics scope shows one app across all its projects.
Alert by searching logs by hand
A log-based metric with an alerting policy
Manual searches catch problems late. A log-based metric alerts automatically.
Run Prometheus servers yourself on GKE
Managed Service for Prometheus
Self-run Prometheus needs storage, scaling and high-availability work. The managed service handles it.

lessons.title: Apigee, API Gateway, Eventarc, Cloud Scheduler and Cloud Tasks
lessons.what: Services for APIs and events: Apigee and API Gateway manage APIs; Eventarc routes events; Cloud Scheduler runs jobs on a timetable; Cloud Tasks queues individual tasks.
lessons.tests: how services expose APIs, react to events and run work later or on a schedule.
rules: Apigee for full API management: developer portals, API keys, quotas, analytics, monetisation and a facade over legacy systems. API Gateway for a simple managed front door to serverless backends.
Eventarc delivers events from Google services, audit logs and Pub/Sub to Cloud Run, GKE and Workflows in the CloudEvents format.
Cloud Scheduler triggers jobs with cron syntax; Cloud Tasks dispatches individual tasks with rate limits, retries and scheduling, where Pub/Sub is for broadcast-style messaging.
traps: API Gateway for a partner portal with monetisation
Apigee
API Gateway has no developer portal or monetisation. Apigee does.
Pub/Sub when each task must call one endpoint at a controlled rate
Cloud Tasks
Pub/Sub broadcasts to subscribers. Cloud Tasks controls the rate and target for each task.
A VM running cron to trigger a nightly job
Cloud Scheduler
A VM kept just for cron costs money and needs patching. Cloud Scheduler is managed.

domains.title: Hybrid and Migration Services
domains.sub: Running Kubernetes everywhere, and moving VMs and databases to Google Cloud.

lessons.title: GKE Enterprise and Cloud Service Mesh
lessons.what: GKE Enterprise (formerly Anthos) manages Kubernetes clusters on Google Cloud, on-premises and in other clouds as one fleet. Cloud Service Mesh, based on Istio, manages traffic and security between services.
lessons.tests: how to run and govern many clusters consistently, and secure service-to-service traffic.
rules: Fleets group clusters; Config Sync applies configuration from Git to all of them; Policy Controller enforces rules such as allowed registries and no public load balancers.
Clusters outside Google Cloud join through the Connect agent; multi-cluster Gateway or Ingress spreads traffic across clusters.
Cloud Service Mesh adds mTLS between services, traffic splitting, retries and per-service telemetry without changing application code.
traps: Manage each on-premises and cloud cluster separately
One fleet with Config Sync
Managing clusters one by one causes drift. A fleet applies the same configuration and policy everywhere.
Every team writes its own service-to-service authentication
Cloud Service Mesh with mTLS
Each team's own authentication is inconsistent and slow to build. The mesh adds mTLS without code changes.
Move every on-premises cluster to the cloud before managing them together
Attach them to the fleet where they run
Fleets manage clusters where they run, so you can govern them before, or without, moving them.

lessons.title: Migration Center, Migrate to Virtual Machines and VMware Engine
lessons.what: Migration Center discovers what you run and estimates cost; Migrate to Virtual Machines moves VMs from VMware, AWS or Azure to Compute Engine; Google Cloud VMware Engine runs VMware itself on Google Cloud.
lessons.tests: the fastest safe path to move existing servers.
rules: Start with Migration Center to inventory servers, map dependencies and estimate total cost of ownership.
Migrate to Virtual Machines streams VM data, lets you test clones before cutover, and keeps rollback possible.
VMware Engine moves VMware workloads with no changes to VMs or tools, which suits a data centre exit on a deadline.
traps: Rebuild every VM by hand on Compute Engine
Migrate to Virtual Machines
Manual rebuilds are slow and error-prone. The migration tool copies VMs and supports testing and rollback.
Refactor VMware apps first because the lease ends next month
Google Cloud VMware Engine, then modernise later
Refactoring takes months. VMware Engine moves VMs unchanged to meet the deadline.
Cut over without testing
Test with clones before cutover
Test clones catch problems before users are affected.

lessons.title: Database Migration Service and Datastream
lessons.what: Database Migration Service moves databases to Cloud SQL and AlloyDB with continuous replication; Datastream captures changes (CDC) from operational databases into BigQuery and Cloud Storage.
lessons.tests: how to move or replicate databases with little downtime.
rules: Database Migration Service supports MySQL, PostgreSQL and SQL Server to Cloud SQL, PostgreSQL to AlloyDB, and Oracle to PostgreSQL with conversion help; it replicates continuously, so downtime is only the final cutover.
Datastream streams inserts, updates and deletes from MySQL, PostgreSQL, Oracle and SQL Server into BigQuery for near real-time analytics.
Self-managed databases you are not ready to change can run on Compute Engine (or, for MongoDB, MongoDB Atlas from the Marketplace).
traps: Dump and restore a busy production database over a weekend
Database Migration Service with continuous replication
A dump stops writes for hours. Continuous replication keeps the target in sync until a short cutover.
Nightly full exports to keep BigQuery up to date
Datastream change data capture
Nightly exports are a day old and heavy. Change data capture streams only the changes, in near real time.
Rewrite an app to move MySQL to Cloud SQL
No rewrite; migrate it as it is
Cloud SQL runs the same MySQL engine, so the app connects with minimal changes.

domains.title: AI and ML Services
domains.sub: Google Cloud's AI platform, ready-made APIs, search and agents.

lessons.title: Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform (formerly Vertex AI)
lessons.what: Google Cloud's unified platform for machine learning, generative AI and agents: models, training, tuning, deployment and monitoring.
lessons.tests: which part of the platform fits the AI requirement.
rules: Model Garden gives Gemini, Imagen and Veo, open models such as Gemma and Llama, and partner models such as Claude. Agent Studio prototypes prompts and agents; the Agent Development Kit (ADK) and Agent Runtime build and run production agents.
AutoML trains models on your labelled data without code; custom training runs your TensorFlow, PyTorch or scikit-learn code on GPUs or TPUs.
Model Registry versions models, endpoints serve them, model monitoring watches for drift, pipelines automate the lifecycle, and Explainable AI shows why a model predicted what it did.
traps: Host an open model on a VM you manage
Deploy it from Model Garden to a managed endpoint
Self-hosting means managing GPUs, scaling and patching. A managed endpoint does the serving for you.
No way to explain a model's decisions to auditors
Explainable AI plus audit logs
Auditors need reasons for predictions. Explainable AI provides them and audit logs record who did what.
Retrain by hand when accuracy drops
Model monitoring with automated retraining pipelines
Manual checks miss drift until users notice. Monitoring can trigger retraining automatically.

lessons.title: Pre-trained AI APIs and BigQuery ML
lessons.what: Ready-made models behind an API (Vision, Video Intelligence, Speech-to-Text, Text-to-Speech, Translation, Natural Language, Document AI) and BigQuery ML for models built in SQL.
lessons.tests: when a standard AI task needs no custom training, or analysts want ML where the data already is.
rules: Vision and Video Intelligence label images and video and detect unsafe content; Speech-to-Text and Text-to-Speech convert speech; Translation and Natural Language handle text; Document AI extracts fields from forms and invoices.
Use the API first; move to AutoML or tuning only when its labels do not fit your business.
BigQuery ML trains and runs models (forecasting, classification, even calls to Gemini) with SQL, with no data movement.
traps: Train a model to read invoices from scratch
Document AI
Document AI already extracts invoice fields. A custom model needs data and time.
Export BigQuery data to a notebook for a simple forecast
BigQuery ML
BigQuery ML forecasts with SQL where the data already is.
Custom training to flag explicit images
Vision API safe search, or Video Intelligence for video
Safe search already detects explicit images. No training needed.

lessons.title: Agent Search, RAG and Gemini Enterprise
lessons.what: Agent Search adds Google-quality search and grounded AI answers to sites and apps; the RAG Engine builds custom retrieval pipelines; Gemini Enterprise gives employees AI search and agents across company data.
lessons.tests: how to ground AI answers in your own data and make internal knowledge searchable.
rules: Agent Search indexes websites, documents and BigQuery data and returns results or generated answers with citations, with little code.
RAG Engine for custom retrieval-augmented generation pipelines; grounding with Google Search for current public information.
Gemini Enterprise (formerly Agentspace) searches Drive, Jira, Confluence, SharePoint and more, respecting each user's permissions, with ready-made and custom agents.
traps: Fine-tune a model on the product manuals so it answers questions
Ground it with Agent Search or RAG
Tuning doesn't reliably add facts, and they go stale. Grounding retrieves the current manual at answer time.
Build a custom search engine for internal documents
Gemini Enterprise or Agent Search
A managed search product is faster to deliver and respects each user's permissions.
Let the model answer from memory about current events
Grounding with Google Search
A model's knowledge stops at its training date. Grounding with Google Search adds current information.

lessons.title: Conversational Agents and Customer Engagement
lessons.what: Dialogflow CX and Conversational Agents build chat and voice agents; Gemini Enterprise for CX (formerly Customer Engagement Suite) adds Agent Assist, conversation insights and a cloud contact centre.
lessons.tests: how to automate support and help human agents.
rules: Conversational Agents (Dialogflow CX) handle multi-turn text and voice conversations on web, mobile and phone, and hand off to people when needed.
Agent Assist suggests replies, knowledge articles and summaries to human agents in real time; Conversational Insights analyses calls for trends and sentiment.
Contact Center as a Service runs voice and chat routing in the cloud with these AI features built in.
traps: Hire more agents for 24/7 routine questions
Conversational Agents for routine requests
Virtual agents handle routine questions around the clock at lower cost.
Build a chatbot from scratch on a foundation model API
Dialogflow CX or Conversational Agents
Dialogflow CX already handles conversation flows, telephony and handoff to people.
Listen to call recordings by hand to find common issues
Conversational Insights
Manual review covers a tiny sample. Conversational Insights analyses every call.

endNote: Good luck on exam day. Find the constraint in each question, prefer the managed option, and answer the case studies from their requirements.
pairWith: Google's official sample questions are the best next step. A PCA practice question bank is on the way; BrainByte subscribers hear first.
